principles.statement: Extract the first balanced, parseable JSON object from an LLM response — scan every '{' as a candidate start with string-aware brace depth, accept the first candidate that both balances AND parses.
principles.rationale: Live-confirmed 2026-09-20: small local models (BitNet i2_s) wrap usable JSON in prompt echo, skip scaffolding, code fences, and hallucinated follow-up instructions; a first-{-to-last-} slice spans all of that noise and fails to parse every single time, burning real retry budget on parseable answers.

principles.statement: Never treat a parse failure as a model failure without checking what the extractor did with the response — the model may have answered correctly inside noise.
principles.rationale: A strict extractor turns a working-but-noisy model into an apparent failure, and the retry loop then burns attempts (and rate budget) on a problem that lives in the caller, not the model.

principles.statement: Extraction tests must use REAL malformed outputs captured from live logs, not hand-invented tidy cases.
principles.rationale: The rescue logic that passes tidy fixtures failed on every real response until the actual BitNet shapes (trailing chatter, `skip:` wrappers, echo+fence+confabulation) became the test corpus.

heuristics.name: Parsing LLM output that should contain a JSON object, especially from small/local models.
heuristics.description: Scan candidate objects left-to-right (string-aware depth tracking); return the first that serde-accepts. Fall back to {} only when no candidate parses.

heuristics.name: Writing a retry loop around an LLM extraction step.
heuristics.description: Log the RAW response on parse failure (truncated is fine) so a capture bug is distinguishable from a model failure in the very next log read.

decision_rules.condition: An LLM response fails to parse as JSON and the raw text contains a balanced object.
decision_rules.action: Run a balanced-brace, string-aware extraction (first parseable candidate) before declaring failure or spending a retry.
